subsystems.name: Reusable launch vehicle
subsystems.role: accelerates the payload to near-orbital velocity, coasts above the atmosphere, then lands under power.
parts: propellant tanks holding liquid methane and liquid oxygen
landing legs or a catch arrangement

subsystems.name: Thermal protection system
subsystems.role: survives re-entry heating that is close to what an orbital vehicle sees, because the coast is near-orbital.

subsystems.name: Payload cabin or cargo bay
subsystems.role: keeps people or freight alive and intact through several g of acceleration, vacuum and vibration.
parts: galley and toilet for short flights

subsystems.name: Point-to-point ground infrastructure
subsystems.role: two distant sites must each launch, catch or land, refuel and service the vehicle quickly.

subsystems.name: Range, tracking and abort systems
subsystems.role: keeps the corridor clear and the vehicle under control over thousands of kilometres of ocean and land.

subsystems.name: Operations and passenger handling
subsystems.role: turns a rocket flight into a repeatable service, from ticketing to boarding to turnaround.

buildSteps.title: Size the vehicle to the route
buildSteps.detail: A near-antipodal hop of around 17,000 km needs the vehicle to reach close to orbital velocity, about 7–8 km/s, so it must be a fully reusable super-heavy rocket rather than a small sounding rocket.

buildSteps.title: Design for re-entry from near-orbital speed
buildSteps.detail: The heat shield is sized for a much harsher entry than a suborbital tourism hop, which drives the whole vehicle's mass and shape.

buildSteps.title: Build and fly the reusable stack
buildSteps.detail: Stainless-steel or composite tanks are welded, engines installed, and the vehicle flown repeatedly to prove that landing and inspection can be done cheaply.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate uncrewed point-to-point delivery
buildSteps.detail: Freight or instrumented payloads are flown between two distant pads to measure landing accuracy, structural loads, noise and turnaround time before any passengers are carried. Military logistics studies have examined exactly this use.

buildSteps.title: Qualify human factors and escape
buildSteps.detail: Seats, restraint, acceleration limits, cabin pressure loss, emergency egress and abort options are tested and certified, since no civil airworthiness code yet covers a rocket airliner.

buildSteps.title: Adapt or build the ground network
buildSteps.detail: Sites must sit far enough from cities to limit noise and blast risk, yet close enough to be useful, with propellant supply at both ends and offshore platforms as one option.

buildSteps.title: Set up the regulatory route
buildSteps.detail: Aviation-style certification, overflight permissions across many countries and a traffic-management regime for high-altitude vehicles are needed before tickets can be sold.

buildSteps.title: Operate a first route
buildSteps.detail: One city pair is flown on a schedule with high-tempo reuse, and cost per seat is driven down by flying each vehicle many times a year.

prerequisites.why: boosters have landed and reflown, but rapid, low-cost reuse of an entire stack is still being proven; the economics of the concept depend on it completely.

prerequisites.tech: Thermal protection that survives near-orbital re-entry repeatedly
prerequisites.why: reusable heat shields work, but tiles still need careful inspection and refurbishment between flights.

prerequisites.tech: Precision propulsive landing at a distant site
prerequisites.why: the vehicle must arrive within metres of a pad after a ballistic arc of thousands of kilometres.
global launch rates are measured in hundreds per year, while an airline-like service needs many flights per site per day.

prerequisites.tech: Passenger certification and airspace rules for rockets
prerequisites.why: no regulator has an airworthiness framework for paying passengers on a suborbital transport flight.
launch and sonic-boom noise currently rule out most sites near the populations that would use the service.

pathway.milestone: reusable super-heavy vehicles in flight test and government studies of rocket-delivered cargo
pathway.unlocks: data on landing accuracy, reuse cost and turnaround time.

pathway.milestone: uncrewed point-to-point flights between two fixed pads, carrying freight or instruments
pathway.unlocks: proof that the trajectory, thermal loads and ground operations work end to end.

pathway.milestone: a crewed demonstration on one route, with test crew and no paying public
pathway.unlocks: human-rating evidence and a first regulatory precedent.

pathway.milestone: a certified commercial route, most likely for time-critical freight and premium passengers
pathway.unlocks: a niche service that can grow only if cost per flight falls far enough to compete with jets.
